# **1 Introduction**  {#1-introduction}

## **1.1 Purpose** {#1.1-purpose}

This report encompasses the functionality, model and design of the web application ‘Trailblazer’, which is meant to serve as a supportive community-based application for users participating in outdoor activities, including hiking, running and walking. This documentation is intended to serve as a tool for any user: 

* investigating the features, scope, as well as database and UI/UX design of the application;   
* researching the best usage methods;  
* extending the features of the application; 

and serves as the primary source of information regarding this project. 

## **1.2 Background** {#1.2-background}

This product serves as a tool for athletes, hobbyists, and beginners in outdoor activities, allowing them to delegate the mundane tasks of researching new trails and walking paths to Trailblazer, which will have a large variety of these paths. This product will also provide users with a community built around their hobbies, allowing them to meet fellow enthusiasts, as well as make new friends with common interests to socialize with, enhancing their sense of community, and driving their motivation and goals forward. This will help them to discover new routes, with experienced adventurers sharing their experiences, tips and reviews of these routes. 

The current market does not have any purpose-built applications similar to the idea of Trailblazer we are keen to develop towards, which serve as a community-driven social application bringing enthusiasts together. All existing applications in this sector currently focus on personal tracking, with many social features locked behind paid subscriptions, limiting users who would otherwise be interested in interacting with other enthusiasts. Many existing social applications in other sectors, such as Facebook and Instagram, allow users to use their core social functionality and features at no-cost, allowing them to bring in a larger audience, while offsetting their economic expenses through the use of online advertisements. As such, a similar avenue built exclusively around outdoor experiences such as hiking and running is uncharted territory.

## **1.3 Scope** {#1.3-scope}

We intend to solve the current empty space in the outdoor adventures sector, which lacks an intended social space for people to connect over recommended routes, paths and experiences. The application, named ‘**Trailblazer**’, would consist of features allowing users to review trails, in the form of posts, allowing other users to comment on those reviews, verifying their authenticity and boosting the reviewer’s profile, personal audience and platform in return. This would allow for a feedback-based system, driven by the community, allowing for self-fueled, sustainable growth for the Trailblazer platform, as well as the community. 

Currently, there exists a space of unverified, inaccurate information on online platforms, regarding the difficulty, access and availability of trails and routes. These discussion boards and forums lack oversight and accountability (Gardner, 2025). By investing into building a social interface behind the sharing of knowledge regarding trails and routes, we would build an accountable, verifiable and accurate knowledge board, accompanied by a social community that helps to expand knowledge of these trails and experiences, instead of the current environment of unverified information. Experienced users sharing tips in their reviews would also help facilitate responsible trekking from future visitors, helping mitigate the damage of the natural habitats surrounding these trails.

**The application of this software would consist of:** 

* reviews, posts, photographs and comments posted by users;   
* trails and routes uploaded by users, including relevant statistics like length, estimated duration, level of difficulty, geographic start and end locations in order to aid future visitors;  
* searching for these trails by keyword and filter search  
* listing of most popular routes logged by members of the community;  
* bookmarking of trails by users to access promptly in the future;  
* logging of completed trails and routes;  
* editing personal profile, including a personal avatar;  
* conferral of badges, indicating achievements of the user;   
* visual analytics are available to the user, aiding them in tracking their personal progress;

## **1.4 Overview** {#1.4-overview}

This documentation includes the functional requirements intended to be realised in this project, including the features we set out to accomplish at the beginning of this project. 

As part of that, this documentation includes the data model we intend to follow in the implementation of the codebase of this project. The data model consists of an entity relationship diagram, also included separately, as well as a cheat-sheet that was designed to aid in the accessible reading of this data model diagram. It also includes the relationships between the tables and columns in the data model, including the cardinality & optionality relating to these tables. This documentation also includes the normalization and key constraints for certain columns in tables in the included data model.

This documentation also includes wireframes we have designed for the benefit of both the project team and anyone utilizing this documentation, that include visual implementations of the webpages to be contained in this application. The webpages include: home, trail search, trail detail, personal profile, and trail upload, among others.  

**How the documentation is organized:**

1. Introduction (current section)  
2. Functional requirements  
3. Data model  
4. Wireframes  
5. References  
6. External link to ERD diagram

# **2 Functional Requirements** {#2-functional-requirements}

This template illustrates a demo for creating a functional requirement that align with the IEEE standards. Please refer to the IEEE Std 830-1998 document if you need any more information and clarifications.

## **FR‑1. Identity & Access Management** {#fr‑1.-identity-&-access-management}

### **FR‑1.1 Account Registration** {#fr‑1.1-account-registration}

* **Description:** The system shall allow a visitor to create an account by submitting username, email, password and consequently log in using validated account details.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Username (3–30 chars, alphanumeric \+ `_`/`.`), email (RFC 5322), password (\>=8 chars).  
* **Sequence:** Create **USERS** record with `email_unverified` state; store salted hash; ensure `USERS.email` and `USERS.username` are unique.  
* **Outputs:** `201 Created` with user id; dispatch email verification token (see FR‑1.2).  
* **Abnormal errors:** `409` on duplicate email/username; `422` on invalid fields

### **FR‑1.2 Email Verification** {#fr‑1.2-email-verification}

* **Description:** The system shall issue a time‑boxed email verification token and confirm the email when the token is presented.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Token (opaque, single‑use, TTL=24 h).  
* **Sequence:** Match token in **EMAIL\_VERIFICATION\_TOKENS** to user; set user’s email status to verified.  
* **Outputs:** Success confirmation and redirect to Login.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `410` on expired token; `404` on invalid token..

### **FR‑1.3 Login** {#fr‑1.3-login}

* **Description:** The system shall authenticate a user with email \+ password and establish a session.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Email (RFC 5322), password; rate‑limit 10 attempts / 15 min / ip+email; email must be verified.  
* **Sequence:** Verify password hash; deny if email not verified; create HTTP‑only, Secure session cookie (TTL 7 days, rolling); update `USERS.last_login_at`.  
* **Outputs:** Authenticated session; return minimal profile (id, public display name from **USER\_PROFILES**, avatar URL).  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` on failure; lock out after 10 failed attempts per 15 min \-\> `429`

### **FR‑1.4 Forgot Password / Reset** {#fr‑1.4-forgot-password-/-reset}

* **Description:** The system shall allow a user to request a password reset email and set a new password using a one‑time token.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Email address; later: reset token \+ new password (\>=8 chars).  
* **Sequence:** Create **PASSWORD\_RESET\_TOKENS** (TTL 1 h); on redemption, rotate password hash and invalidate token(s).  
* **Outputs:** Email‑sent acknowledgement; success page on reset.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `410`/`404` on expired/invalid token. 

### **FR‑1.5 Session Termination** {#fr‑1.5-session-termination}

* **Description**: The system shall allow an authenticated user to log out, invalidating the active session token.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Current session cookie; optional `all_sessions=true` to log out from all devices.  
* **Sequence:** Invalidate session server‑side; if `all_sessions=true`, revoke all active sessions for the user; clear client cookie.  
* **Outputs:** `204 No Content`.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` if no active session; `500` on server revocation failure.

## **FR‑2. Trail Discovery & Search** {#fr‑2.-trail-discovery-&-search}

### **FR‑2.1 Keyword Search** {#fr‑2.1-keyword-search}

* **Description:** The system shall return a paginated list of **TRAILS** matching a free‑text query over trail name, location, and description.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `q` (0–120 chars), `page`, `page_size` (\<=50).  
* **Sequence:** Full‑text/ILIKE search; only `approval_state='approved'` trails are eligible; default sort by popularity (see FR‑9.2).  
* **Outputs:** List with fields: id, name, primary photo URL, location (city/country), distance, difficulty, rating summary.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `422` on invalid page size. 

### **FR‑2.2 Structured Filters** {#fr‑2.2-structured-filters}

* **Description:** The system shall filter search results by difficulty, distance range, category, and city/country.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Optional filters: `difficulty∈{Easy,Moderate,Hard}`; `distance_km_min/max` (0–2000, `min≤max`); `category_ids[]` (\<=10); `city`/`country` (\<=80 chars).  
* **Sequence:** Apply intersection of provided filters atop FR‑2.1 results; combine with pagination; cache last used filters per session for UX continuity.  
* **Outputs:** Filtered list; include `total_count` for the query.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `422` on invalid enums/ranges; `413` if too many `category_ids`; `400` if `distance_km_min>distance_km_max`

### **FR‑2.3 Map Results** {#fr‑2.3-map-results}

* **Description:** The system shall return geo‑coordinates for visible results and a bounding‑box aggregate for map rendering and clustering.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `bbox` (south, west, north, east), `zoom` (0–22), optional `cluster=true`, `max_markers` (\<=500).  
* **Sequence:** Filter **TRAILS** within `bbox` (approved only); compute clusters (e.g., geohash/grid) based on `zoom`; compute bounds of returned set; limit non‑clustered markers to `max_markers`.  
* **Outputs:** For each item: `id`, `lat`, `lng`, `name`, `is_cluster`, `cluster_count` (if clustered). Response includes `map_bounds` and `total_in_bbox`.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `422` on malformed `bbox`/`zoom`; `413` if `max_markers` exceeded when `cluster=false`

## **FR‑3. Trail Viewing & Media** {#fr‑3.-trail-viewing-&-media}

### **FR‑3.1 Trail Detail** {#fr‑3.1-trail-detail}

* **Description:** The system shall return a trail by id/slug with full details: name, description, city/country, distance, difficulty, GPX/geometry (if any), categories, creator, approval state, and aggregated stats (rating, saves, views).  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `id` or `slug`; only approved trails are publicly viewable; creators and staff may view their own `pending/rejected` trails.  
* **Sequence:** Fetch **TRAILS** \+ join **TRAIL\_CATEGORIES**, **TRAIL\_STATS**, creator (**USERS/USER\_PROFILES**), and primary photo from **TRAIL\_PHOTOS**; authorize if not approved; include related “similar trails” (same category/city, top 5).  
* **Outputs:** JSON detail; includes rating summary (avg \+ count), save count, view count, and whether the signed‑in user has saved/completed it.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `404` if not found or not authorized; `403` if viewing unapproved trail without permission.

### **FR‑3.2 Photos** {#fr‑3.2-photos}

* **Description:** The system shall return all photos for a trail and indicate exactly one `is_primary=true`.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `trail_id`; enforce “one primary photo” per trail via unique partial index.  
* **Sequence:** Query **TRAIL\_PHOTOS** by `trail_id`; order primary first, then by creation time.  
* **Outputs:** Array of `{photo_id, url, caption, is_primary, uploader_id}`.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `404` if `trail_id` unknown

### **FR‑3.3 View Tracking** {#fr‑3.3-view-tracking}

* **Description:** The system shall create a **VIEWS** record when a trail detail is rendered.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `trail_id`, optional `user_id`, client fingerprint/IP (for dedupe).  
* **Sequence:** On detail render (server event), upsert at most 1 view per user/device per trail per 30 minutes; enqueue counter update to **TRAIL\_STATS** (FR‑9.1).  
* **Outputs:** No body (`204`); counters feed FR‑9.2.  
* **Abnormal errors:** None user‑visible; log internal `5xx` failures; do not block page render

## **FR‑4. Comments & Ratings**  {#fr‑4.-comments-&-ratings}

### **FR‑4.1 Create Comment / Optional Rating** {#fr‑4.1-create-comment-/-optional-rating}

* **Description:** The system shall allow an authenticated user to post a comment on a trail with an optional star rating (1–5).  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `trail_id`, `body` (1–1,000 chars) and/or `rating∈[1..5]`; at most one rating per user per trail (unique partial constraint); comments may be threaded via `parent_id` or `NULL`.  
* **Sequence:** Authorize user; validate inputs; enforce “one rating per user/trail”; persist in **COMMENTS**; update **TRAIL\_STATS** (avg, count) and **USER\_STATS**.  
* **Outputs:** `201 Created` with `{comment_id, created_at, rating, body}`.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `403` if unauthenticated; `404` if trail not found; `422` on invalid fields; `409` if rating already exists.

### **FR‑4.2 Edit/Delete Own Comment** {#fr‑4.2-edit/delete-own-comment}

* **Description:** The system shall allow the author to edit or delete their own comment; edits retain last‑edited timestamp and version.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `comment_id`; for edit: `body` (1–1,000 chars) and/or `rating` change; for delete: `hard=false` (soft‑delete) by default.  
* **Sequence:** Check ownership or staff role; for edits, write new version row or persist `edited_at` and `version`; if rating changed/removed, recompute **TRAIL\_STATS**.  
* **Outputs:** `200 OK` with updated comment (edit) or `204 No Content` (delete).  
* **Abnormal errors:** `403` if not owner; `404` if comment not found; `409` if edit violates rating uniqueness. 

### **FR‑4.3 List Comments** {#fr‑4.3-list-comments}

* **Description:** The system shall paginate comments for a trail, sorted by recency or helpfulness (rating present \> no rating, then newest).  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `trail_id`, `sort∈{newest,helpful}`, `page`, `page_size` (\<=50).  
* **Sequence:** Query **COMMENTS** by `trail_id` with selected sort; include author display name/avatar from **USER\_PROFILES**; include whether the viewer authored each comment.  
* **Outputs:** Page of comments with `{id, body, rating, parent_id, created_at, edited_at, author{display_name,avatar}}` and `total_count`.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `404` if `trail_id` unknown; `422` on invalid `page_size`.

## **FR‑5. Personalization: Bookmarks & Completions** {#fr‑5.-personalization:-bookmarks-&-completions}

### **FR‑5.1 Bookmark Toggle (“Save”)** {#fr‑5.1-bookmark-toggle-(“save”)}

* **Description:** The system shall let a signed‑in user add/remove a bookmark for a trail.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `trail_id`; composite key uniqueness `(user_id, trail_id)`; idempotent toggling.  
* **Sequence:** If not present, insert into **BOOKMARKS**; else delete; update `save_count` in **TRAIL\_STATS** and **USER\_STATS**.  
* **Outputs:** `200 OK` with `{saved: true|false, total_saves}`.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` if not authenticated; `404` if trail not found; `409` on race/duplicate insert.

### **FR‑5.2 Log Completion** {#fr‑5.2-log-completion}

* **Description:** The system shall let a user record a trail completion with `completed_at` (default: now) and optional notes/duration.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `trail_id`, `completed_at` (ISO), `notes` (\<=500), `duration_min` (0–10,000); composite PK `(user_id, trail_id, completed_at)` allows multiple completions.  
* **Sequence:** Insert into **COMPLETIONS**; update **USER\_STATS**; evaluate badges (FR‑8.1).  
* **Outputs:** `201 Created` with completion id/timestamp.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` unauthenticated; `404` unknown trail; `422` invalid fields.

### **FR‑5.3 Unlog/Amend Completion** {#fr‑5.3-unlog/amend-completion}

* **Description:** The system shall allow a user to delete a completion entry or edit its note/duration within 24 hours of creation.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `completion_id`; for edit: new `notes`/`duration_min`; edits allowed \<=24 h from `created_at`.  
* **Sequence:** Authorize ownership; if within window, update; else only delete; update **USER\_STATS**; recompute badge progress.  
* **Outputs:** `200 OK` with updated entry or `204 No Content` on delete.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `403` if outside edit window or not owner; `404` if entry not found. 

### **FR‑5.4 My Saves & My Completions** {#fr‑5.4-my-saves-&-my-completions}

* **Description:** The system shall provide endpoints to list the signed‑in user’s saved trails and completion history (with pagination and filters).  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `page`, `page_size` (\<=50); optional filters: `city/country`, `difficulty`, `date_range` for completions.  
* **Sequence:** Query **BOOKMARKS**/**COMPLETIONS** joined to **TRAILS** and **TRAIL\_PHOTOS** (primary).  
* **Outputs:** Paginated lists with counts; each item includes trail summary and user‑specific metadata (saved/completed state).  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` unauthenticated; `422` invalid `page_size`.

## **FR‑6. Content Authoring: Trails & Photos**   {#fr‑6.-content-authoring:-trails-&-photos}

### **FR‑6.1 Create Trail** {#fr‑6.1-create-trail}

* **Description:** The system shall allow a signed‑in user to create a trail with: name, description (\<=2,000 chars), distance (km), difficulty, city, country, latitude, longitude, and categories (0..N).  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Name (3–120 chars), description (\<=2,000), `distance_km>0`, `difficulty∈{Easy,Moderate,Hard}`, `city`/`country` (\<=80 chars), `lat∈[-90,90]`, `lng∈[-180,180]`, `category_ids[]` (\<=10).  
* **Sequence:** Persist **TRAILS** with `approval_state='pending'` and `creator_id=user.id`; generate unique `slug`; insert **TRAIL\_CATEGORIES**; enqueue “needs primary photo” check (must be set before approval—FR‑6.2).  
* **Outputs:** `201 Created` with `{trail_id, slug, approval_state:'pending'}`.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` unauthenticated; `422` invalid fields; `409` duplicate slug.

### **FR‑6.2 Upload Photos** {#fr‑6.2-upload-photos}

* **Description:** The system shall allow the creator (or authorized contributors) to upload one or more **TRAIL\_PHOTOS** and set one as primary.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `trail_id`, image file(s) (\<=10 MB each; types: JPEG/PNG/WebP), optional `caption` (\<=140); primary must be set before approval.  
* **Sequence:** Authorize uploader; store object(s); create **TRAIL\_PHOTOS** rows; if `is_primary=true`, enforce unique‑partial index to keep exactly one primary.  
* **Outputs:** `201 Created` with list of uploaded photos and `primary_photo_id`.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` unauthenticated; `403` if not creator/staff; `404` unknown trail; `422` invalid file; `409` if two photos marked primary.

### **FR‑6.3 Edit/Delete Own Trail** {#fr‑6.3-edit/delete-own-trail}

* **Description:** The system shall allow the creator to edit or delete their trail while it is `pending` or `rejected`.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `trail_id`; editable fields as in FR‑6.1; deletion is disabled for `approved` trails (locked).  
* **Sequence:** Authorize creator or staff; if state `approved`, return `409`; else apply changes or soft‑delete; maintain **TRAIL\_CATEGORIES** integrity.  
* **Outputs:** `200 OK` with updated trail or `204 No Content` on delete.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401`/`403` unauthorized; `404` not found; `409` edit conflict with locked state. 

### **FR‑6.4 Ownership & Permissions** {#fr‑6.4-ownership-&-permissions}

* **Description:** The system shall restrict trail updates to the creator or staff roles; photo delete restricted to uploader/creator or staff.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Current user role; `trail_id`/`photo_id`.  
* **Sequence:** Check role/ownership against **USERS**, **TRAILS**, **TRAIL\_PHOTOS**; proceed or deny.  
* **Outputs:** `204 No Content` on success.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `403` forbidden; `404` if resource missing.

## **FR‑7. Profiles & Settings**  {#fr‑7.-profiles-&-settings}

### **FR‑7.1 View Public Profile** {#fr‑7.1-view-public-profile}

* **Description:** The system shall display a user’s public profile with avatar, display name, bio, experience, and public stats (created trails, completions, comments, bookmarks) and earned badges.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `username` or `user_id`; only public fields from **USER\_PROFILES/USER\_STATS/USER\_BADGES** are shown.  
* **Sequence:** Resolve profile; aggregate counts from **USER\_STATS** and badges from **USER\_BADGES**; list up to 10 latest created trails.  
* **Outputs:** Profile JSON used by the public profile page.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `404` if profile not found. 

### **FR‑7.2 Edit Profile** {#fr‑7.2-edit-profile}

* **Description:** The system shall allow a signed‑in user to edit their profile (display name ≤50 chars, bio ≤500 chars, experience enum) and upload an avatar image.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `display_name` (3–50), `bio` (\<=500), `experience∈{Beginner,Intermediate,Advanced}`, avatar file (\<=5 MB JPEG/PNG/WebP).  
* **Sequence:** Authorize user; validate; update **USER\_PROFILES**; regenerate public profile cache.  
* **Outputs:** `200 OK` with updated profile fields.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` unauthenticated; `422` invalid fields/file

### **FR‑7.3 My Dashboard**  {#fr‑7.3-my-dashboard}

* **Description:** The system shall present a signed‑in user with a dashboard summarizing **USER\_STATS** (totals of created trails, completions, comments, bookmarks).  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** None (auth required).  
* **Sequence:** Read **USER\_STATS**; compute delta vs last 7/30 days; include shortcuts to FR‑5.4 lists.  
* **Outputs:** Dashboard JSON with counters and trend deltas.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` unauthenticated. 

## **FR‑8. Badges & Achievements**  {#fr‑8.-badges-&-achievements}

### **FR‑8.1 Award Badges Automatically** {#fr‑8.1-award-badges-automatically}

* **Description:** The system shall evaluate **BADGES** criteria on relevant events (e.g., first completion, 10 completions, first trail created) and create **USER\_BADGES** when criteria are met.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Triggered by events: completion logged (FR‑5.2), trail created (FR‑6.1), etc.  
* **Sequence:** On event, evaluate rules; if satisfied and not previously awarded, insert **USER\_BADGES**; update profile cache; send in‑app notification.  
* **Outputs:** Badge appears on profile; notification payload.  
* **Abnormal errors:** None user‑visible; log errors and retry via job

### **FR‑8.2 List My Badges** {#fr‑8.2-list-my-badges}

* **Description:** The system shall let a signed‑in user view their earned badges and criteria progress toward next badges.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Auth required; `page_size` (≤50).  
* **Sequence:** Query **USER\_BADGES**; compute progress percentages from **USER\_STATS**.  
* **Outputs:** List of badges with `{name, icon, earned_at}` and progress indicators.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `401` unauthenticated.

## **FR‑9. Analytics**  {#fr‑9.-analytics}

### **FR‑9.1 Maintain Counters** {#fr‑9.1-maintain-counters}

* **Description:** The system shall maintain **TRAIL\_STATS** (views, saves, average rating, ratings count) and **USER\_STATS** via event‑driven updates (on view, bookmark toggle, comment/rating create/update/delete, trail create).  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Events from FR‑3.3, FR‑4.*, FR‑5.*, FR‑6.1.  
* **Sequence:** On event, update denormalized counters; store daily rollups for 7/30/90‑day windows.  
* **Outputs:** Updated stats rows used by FR‑2/FR‑9.2.  
* **Abnormal errors:** Log and retry via background job; do not block user actions. .

### **FR‑9.2 Popular/Explore Feeds** {#fr‑9.2-popular/explore-feeds}

* **Description:** The system shall expose endpoints to list trails sorted by most viewed and most saved over rolling windows (e.g., 7/30 days) using **TRAIL\_STATS**.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** `sort∈{most_viewed,most_saved,top_rated}`, `window∈{7d,30d,all}`, `page`, `page_size` (\<=50).  
* **Sequence:** Read **TRAIL\_STATS** aggregates; apply window; sort; paginate.  
* **Outputs:** Paginated list for the Explore page with summary metrics per trail.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `422` invalid sort/window; `503` if aggregates unavailable.

## **FR‑10. Error Handling & System Feedback**  {#fr‑10.-error-handling-&-system-feedback}

### **FR‑10.1 User‑Friendly Error Pages** {#fr‑10.1-user‑friendly-error-pages}

* **Description:** The system shall render a branded error page for unhandled errors and missing routes, with a control to return to Home.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Any unhandled `4xx/5xx` or unmatched route.  
* **Sequence:** Capture error; render error UI per wireframe; include request id for support.  
* **Outputs:** HTML error page; “Back to Home” link.  
* **Abnormal errors:** N/A (this is the abnormal path itself). *(See error wireframe.)*

### **FR‑10.2 Validation Errors** {#fr‑10.2-validation-errors}

* **Description:** The system shall return field‑level validation messages for `4xx` errors with machine‑readable codes and human‑readable hints.  
* **Inputs & Constraints:** Any API request with invalid inputs.  
* **Sequence:** Validate; on failure, return `{code, field, message}` per error.  
* **Outputs:** `422` response with array of errors; UI highlights invalid fields.  
* **Abnormal errors:** `400` for malformed JSON; `413` for payload too large.

# **3\. Data Model** {#3.-data-model}

![][image2]

## **Entity cheat-sheet** {#entity-cheat-sheet}

* **USERS** – accounts/credentials, roles, email verification state.  
* **USER\_PROFILES** – public profile (display name, avatar, bio, experience).  
* **USER\_STATS** – cached totals per user (created trails, completions, comments, bookmarks).  
* **PASSWORD\_RESET\_TOKENS** – secure tokens for “Forgot password”.  
* **EMAIL\_VERIFICATION\_TOKENS** – tokens for email confirmation.  
* **TRAILS** – a hike/trail post (location, distance, difficulty, moderation fields).  
* **TRAIL\_PHOTOS** – photos per trail; exactly one is\_primary via unique partial index.  
* **CATEGORIES** – trail categories/tags.  
* **TRAIL\_CATEGORIES** – junction table (N–N) between trails and categories.  
* **COMMENTS** – discussion \+ optional star rating (1..5) per user/trail (one rating per user per trail).  
* **VIEWS** – per-view analytics (user optional for anonymous).  
* **TRAIL\_STATS** – materialized counters for Popular/Explore (“most views/saved”, rating).  
* **BOOKMARKS** – “Save” toggle (drives “most saved”).  
* **COMPLETIONS** – user logged completions (for badges/analytics).  
* **BADGES** – badge catalogue \+ criteria.  
* **USER\_BADGES** – awarded badges to users.  
* **CONTENT\_FLAGS** – moderation flags across trails, comments, and articles (polymorphic target).

## **Relationships \- cardinality & optionality** {#relationships---cardinality-&-optionality}

* **USERS – USER\_PROFILES (1 to 1\)** – mandatory profile per user (**PK=FK**).  
* **USERS – USER\_STATS (1 to 1\)** – one stats row per user (**PK=FK**). *If created later: (1 to 0..1) – optional.*  
* **USERS – PASSWORD\_RESET\_TOKENS (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **USERS – EMAIL\_VERIFICATION\_TOKENS (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **USERS – TRAILS (creator) (1 to 0..N)** – each trail requires a creator.  
* **USERS – TRAILS (approver)** – per user: **1 to 0..N** approved trails; per trail: **0..1** approver (may be unapproved).  
* **TRAILS – TRAIL\_PHOTOS (1 to 0..N)** – business rule: approved trail must have ≥1 photo; is\_primary unique per trail.  
* **USERS – TRAIL\_PHOTOS (uploader) (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **TRAILS – COMMENTS (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **USERS – COMMENTS (author) (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **COMMENTS (parent) – COMMENTS (replies) (1 to 0..N)** – top-level comments have parent\_id \= NULL.  
* **TRAILS – VIEWS (1 to 0..N)** – each view belongs to exactly one trail.  
* **USERS – VIEWS (0..1 to 0..N)** – user\_id nullable to allow anonymous views.  
* **TRAILS – BOOKMARKS (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **USERS – BOOKMARKS (1 to 0..N)** – composite PK (user\_id, trail\_id).  
* **TRAILS – TRAIL\_CATEGORIES (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **CATEGORIES – TRAIL\_CATEGORIES (1 to 0..N)** – composite PK (trail\_id, category\_id); overall **N–N**.  
* **USERS – COMPLETIONS (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **TRAILS – COMPLETIONS (1 to 0..N)** – composite PK (user\_id, trail\_id, completed\_at).  
* **BADGES – USER\_BADGES (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **USERS – USER\_BADGES (1 to 0..N)** – composite PK (user\_id, badge\_id).  
* **TRAILS – TRAIL\_STATS (1 to 1\)** – if auto-created; *otherwise use (1 to 0..1)*.  
* **USERS – CONTENT\_FLAGS (flagged\_by) (1 to 0..N)**.  
* **USERS – CONTENT\_FLAGS (resolved\_by) (0..1 to 0..N)**.  
* **TRAILS – CONTENT\_FLAGS (1 to 0..N)** when target\_type='trail'.  
* **COMMENTS – CONTENT\_FLAGS (1 to 0..N)** when target\_type='comment'.

## **Normalization & key constraints**  {#normalization-&-key-constraints}

* **3NF**: repeating groups factored into junctions (TRAIL\_CATEGORIES), counters separated (TRAIL\_STATS, USER\_STATS).  
* **Composite PKs**: TRAIL\_CATEGORIES(trail\_id, category\_id), BOOKMARKS(user\_id, trail\_id), COMPLETIONS(user\_id, trail\_id, completed\_at), USER\_BADGES(user\_id, badge\_id).  
* **Unique constraints**: USERS.email, USERS.username, TRAILS.slug, CATEGORIES.slug, ARTICLES.slug.  
* **Business rules via indexes**:  
  * One primary photo per trail: UNIQUE(trail\_id) WHERE is\_primary.  
  * One rating per user/trail: UNIQUE(trail\_id, user\_id) WHERE rating IS NOT NULL.

# **4 Wireframes**  {#4-wireframes}

## **4.1 Hiking trail display pages** {#4.1-hiking-trail-display-pages}

### **4.1.1 Home page** {#4.1.1-home-page}

TrailBlazer's homepage is simple and elegant. In the upper left corner is the website logo and a search box. Users can search for hiking routes, locations, and cities by clicking the search box. Clicking the logo returns them to the homepage. A login button is located in the upper right corner. The main section of the homepage features popular hiking routes, and below that is a map showing nearby hiking routes. At the top is the website's slogan and promotional photos. Clicking the Explore Trails button takes you to the Popular Trails section. \[FR-9.2\]*![][image3]*

### **4.1.2 Search Trails page** {#4.1.2-search-trails-page}

Users can search for trails through the search interface by entering keywords including city, location, trail name, etc. \[FR-2\]![][image4]

### **4.1.3 Trail detail page** {#4.1.3-trail-detail-page}

Through the Trail detail page, users can intuitively see the hiking location and route through the map component. Users can also comment and interact in the reviews section below. \[FR-3\]![][image5]

### **4.1.4 Profile page** {#4.1.4-profile-page}

Through the Profile page, users can see their published trials and their own user information, including avatar, bio, etc. \[FR-7.1\]

![][image6]

### **4.1.5 Profile setting page** {#4.1.5-profile-setting-page}

Users can modify their personal information through the Profile setting page. \[FR-7.1\]

![][image7]

## **4.2 Hiking registration pages** {#4.2-hiking-registration-pages}

### **4.2.1 Login page** {#4.2.1-login-page}

Users can log in by using their registered email and password on the Login page. \[FR-1.3\]

![][image8]

### **4.2.2 Create account page** {#4.2.2-create-account-page}

Users can register through the Create account page. By entering their username, email, and password. \[FR-1.1\]

![][image9]

### **4.2.3 Email Confirmation page** {#4.2.3-email-confirmation-page}

The Email Confirmation page will send a verification email to the user's email address during registration to confirm the user's email address. \[FR-1.2\]

![][image10]

### **4.2.4 Forgot password page** {#4.2.4-forgot-password-page}

The Forgot password page will guide users to solve the problem of forgetting their passwords, and verify their identity through email. \[FR-1.4\]

![][image11]

## **4.3 Hiking trail upload pages** {#4.3-hiking-trail-upload-pages}

### **4.3.1 Upload trail page** {#4.3.1-upload-trail-page}

Through the Hiking trail upload pages, users can upload their own trails by entering the trail name, distance, difficulty level, city, country, latitude and longitude, and description. \[FR-6\]![][image12]

### **4.3.2 Upload success page** {#4.3.2-upload-success-page}

The Upload success page will provide feedback to the user, telling them that the trail has been successfully uploaded. \[FR-6.1\]

![][image13]

## **4.4 Website error pages** {#4.4-website-error-pages}

### **4.4.1 Error Page** {#4.4.1-error-page}

If the website fails, the website will direct the user to the Website error pages to avoid the original error code directly facing the user. Users can also return to the home page by clicking the Back to home button. \[FR-10\]

![][image14]
